subtopic: CUDA / mma.sync — matrix operand layout and warp-level cooperation
learningObjective: Understand the warp-cooperative nature of mma.sync and the register-fragment layout it requires.
stem: Which statement about a Tensor Core `mma.sync` instruction (e.g., `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.f16.f16.f32`) is correct?

options.text: `mma.sync` is a warp-cooperative instruction: all 32 threads in a warp jointly execute one MMA, each holding a fragment of the operands and accumulator in registers per a hardware-defined layout; a single thread cannot execute an mma on its own.
`mma.sync` is a per-thread instruction: each of 32 lanes independently multiplies its 16×8 block by its 8×16 block, so the warp effectively performs 32 independent MMAs per cycle.
`mma.sync` reads its operands directly from global memory and writes accumulators back to global memory; register fragments are only used for the FP32 accumulator.
`mma.sync` requires operands to reside in shared memory; the compiler automatically issues `ldmatrix` to fetch them and reissues the mma on every register-file eviction to avoid stalls.

explanation: Tensor Core `mma.sync` instructions are warp-cooperative: a single mma reads a fixed-shape matrix (e.g., 16×16 for `m16n8k16`) that is distributed across the warp's 32 lanes' registers per a hardware-mandated fragment layout. Individual lanes hold only pieces of the operands and produce pieces of the accumulator. The operands must be in registers at issue time; loading from SMEM uses `ldmatrix` (a warp-cooperative load that produces the required layout), and from GMEM typically goes via `cp.async` → SMEM → `ldmatrix`.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: warp-cooperative execution with fragment layout in registers.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: it is not 32 independent MMAs; it is one warp-wide MMA.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: operands must be in registers, not global memory.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: `mma.sync` requires register operands; `ldmatrix` is a separate instruction used by the programmer.

assumptions: Ampere+ mma.sync instruction set as documented in PTX ISA.
nonImplications: Does not imply that all mma shapes have the same operand layout; different m/n/k tuples use different fragment layouts.
Does not imply that `ldmatrix` is auto-inserted by the CUDA compiler; libraries like CUTLASS emit it explicitly.
